rules:
Internal-representation probe, Paper 2 (CourtDyn). Written before any hidden state is extracted.

QUESTION. Do the adapters' hidden states carry the magnitude of motion as image-plane displacement
(pixels) or as floor-plane motion (metres)? The paper's behavioural claim is that ordering is read
and the unit is not applied; this asks what scale the internal magnitude is on.

MODELS (nf4, frozen protocol loader: eval/run_bench.load_model settings, max_pixels 200704,
enable_thinking=False, prompt = question + GENERATION_SUFFIX): Qwen3.5-4B base (851bf6e8);
courtdyn-native-sft; courtdyn-revision-v3-eventholdout-s42 (v3); courtdyn-mixunit-v3-s42 (mixunit).

ITEMS. All 280 speed+path items of five clips, each asked with the explicit METRE prompt of the
2026-09-12 control protocol (tools/prepare_courtdyn_revision_experiments.py CONTEXT with the height
prior + "in meters (per second)"): Q2_top_480-510 and Q1_top_0-30 (overhead; K = px/m ~27),
Q1_side_0-30 (side; K ~18; HELD OUT for base, v3, mixunit; a TRAINING clip for native),
Q2_side_300-330 and Q4_side_570-600 (side; training clips for native, v3 and mixunit; descriptive
only), plus Q2_top_480-510 with first-frame x4 (null condition). Targets per item, computed
deterministically: metric reference (v3 court homography, engine.court_homography.recompute_answer)
and image-plane displacement in rendered pixels (tools/build_courtdyn_ruler.px_answer); K_i = px/m.

FEATURES. One forward pass on the prompt (no generation needed for features); hidden states at
layers 4, 8, ..., 32; two poolings: mean over image tokens ("img") and the last prompt token
("last"). The metre answer is also generated (greedy, max_new_tokens 16) for the descriptive
behavioural analysis only.

PROBE. Ridge on standardised features; target log(value + eps), eps = 0.05 m(/s) for metres and
0.05*27.3 for pixels; alpha from {1e0..1e5} by inner grouped CV; groups = (clip, 2-s window start).
Out-of-fold predictions on the overhead clips are linearly recalibrated (fit on overhead only).
FEATURE SELECTION, once per model and before any side-view or first-frame feature is scored: the
(layer, pooling) with the highest 5-fold grouped-CV R^2 for the log-metric target on the two
overhead clips, averaged over the two families.

H1 decodability (per model x family): grouped-CV Spearman on the overhead clips >= 0.30 AND above
the 99th percentile of 200 within-clip label permutations.
H3 motion dependence: the probe fit on all overhead full-frame items, applied to Q2_top
first-frame x4 features: "motion-dependent" if rho_static4 <= rho_full(Q2_top, out-of-fold) - 0.30.
H2 image-plane vs floor-plane (the decisive test; base, v3, mixunit; native excluded because it
trained on Q1_side): fit the log-METRE probe on all overhead items (recalibrated), predict Q1_side.
Delta = median over Q1_side items of (log pred - log m_true). The pixel reading predicts
Delta ~= E = median of log(K_i / K_top) over Q1_side items (K_top = median K of the overhead items,
~ log(18/27) ~ -0.4); the metric reading predicts Delta ~= 0. Cell verdict: "image-plane" if
Delta < E/2, else "floor-plane"; 95% bootstrap CI over Q1_side windows (B = 2000).
VALIDITY GUARD: a cell is interpreted only if H1 holds for it and the same probe transfers between
the two OVERHEAD clips (fit Q2_top, predict Q1_top) with |Delta_ctrl| < |E|/2; otherwise UNTESTABLE.
Model verdict over the two families: both image-plane -> image-plane; both floor-plane ->
floor-plane; otherwise mixed.
H4: mixunit and v3 receive the same H2 verdict in each family -> "mixed-unit supervision does not
change the scale on which magnitude is encoded".

INTERPRETATION fixed now. Image-plane for v3/mixunit supports the paper's reading that the order is
read from image-plane motion and the unit is attached afterwards; floor-plane would contradict that
reading and is reported as such. A linear probe shows what is linearly decodable, not what the
model uses; decodability of metres from pixels plus visible scale cues is possible in principle,
which is why H2 tests the transfer of an overhead-trained scale to a view with a different K
rather than within-clip decodability.

DESCRIPTIVE (no verdict): per clip, partial Spearman of the metre ANSWER with pixels given metres
and with metres given pixels (Q1_side primary); within-clip CV decodability of log px vs log m on
Q2_side / Q4_side (training clips).
